title: Prove exact fixed-rank Gaussian inverse error (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration. For the original untruncated varying-phase Gaussian cell of JoyboyBrian / PR5183, at fixed alpha>0 and every fixed rank r>=0:

```text
best rank-at-most-r inverse error / inverse operator norm
    -> 1 / sqrt(2 floor(r/2)+1), as theta -> 0.
```

The complete half-line singular system is explicit: s_k(T_b)=1/(2 sqrt(b(2k+1))). The two boundary layers duplicate every singular value. Rank one therefore cannot lower the limiting relative error; the limiting operator needs rank four to attain relative error at most one half. Arbitrary linear approximants may mix both edges. Only research/gaussian-inverse-rank-error/ is added. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit JoyboyBrian / [PR5183](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5183) for the cited two-edge operator-norm limit and coefficient; Jose Manuel / PR4193, Vlado Vojdanovski / PR1673, Ryanson Jonathan / PR4435, Nick Petalas / PR5150, Cinna Davis and the retained Gaussian lineage. Classical Hermite completeness and derivative identities are cited to [NIST DLMF 1.18.42](https://dlmf.nist.gov/1.18#E42) and [18.9.26](https://dlmf.nist.gov/18.9#E26). No general literature priority is claimed for Hermite singular systems, rank minimax or perturbation inequalities. The new source-specific consequence is the exact full-cell rank-error asymptote. The predecessor's scientific replay is not a deliverable and was not rerun.

[Proof and limits](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4e443f95b29233a03e9cbb496bd645e469973fed/research/gaussian-inverse-rank-error/PROOF.md), [verifier](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4e443f95b29233a03e9cbb496bd645e469973fed/research/gaussian-inverse-rank-error/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4e443f95b29233a03e9cbb496bd645e469973fed/research/gaussian-inverse-rank-error/SOURCES.json), [advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19363381).

## Evidence

Before, the cited source determines the leading inverse norm through its half-line limit. After, the written Hermite argument determines every fixed singular index and the exact rank-error law. Rank-nullity proves optimality against arbitrary approximants; norm perturbation transfers the result to the finite matrix.

Both registered commands pass locally on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only. Warning-strict direct normal and optimized runs took 0.137 and 0.146 seconds and produced identical generated JSON receipts. These are validation durations, not a runtime speedup claim. Each run enumerates 34 Hermite polynomial definitions, 33 weighted derivatives, 512 Gaussian Gram entries, 16 antiderivatives and singular normalizations, 81 coherent mixtures, 1,275 coordinate truncations, 324 rational tolerances, 33 rank-one matrices mixing edge modes and 15 rejection/semantic controls. Finite checks corroborate the written proof; they do not establish completeness or the predecessor limit by sampling.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/gaussian-inverse-rank-error/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/gaussian-inverse-rank-error/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-inverse-rank-error
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/gaussian-inverse-rank-error --check-source-history
```

Substitute the local Python 3.12 path on another host. The expected tokens are PASS_GAUSSIAN_INVERSE_RANK_ERROR, PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE and PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES. The direct verifier can create a hash-bound receipt exclusively outside the checkout with --receipt /absolute/path.json. Metadata, all seven committed package/input files and declared source ancestry pass at head 4e443f95b29233a03e9cbb496bd645e469973fed. AST/in-memory compilation and staged whitespace checks pass. The maximum new function length is 30 lines.

Canonical main was refreshed unchanged at 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, priority revision 8, selected PR6030. The original card scope is explicitly changed to this analytic side result. Cached overlap covered 431 open PRs, 6,406 discussion records and 8,917 local note records, with complete inventories reported by the helper. Direct formula/object searches, merged PR searches and latest claims supplemented it. Arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits.

## Limitations

The limit fixes r and alpha before theta shrinks. No uniform growing-rank or growing-alpha conclusion follows. The limiting-operator least rank is 2 ceil((epsilon^(-2)-1)/2); at equality thresholds this is not an eventual finite-matrix least-rank assertion. The all-size claim depends on the written proof, classical Hermite completeness and the cited PR5183 theorem. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

No mode/coefficient preparation, inverse-application algorithm, rounded-prefix analysis, precision/tape/storage/movement cost, dirty restoration, stock, native/compiler admission, integer recovery or complete multiplication theorem is supplied. Lean, Docker and the selected scientific cold replay were not run. The selected frontier and its five framework assumptions remain unchanged.

## Open next questions

Can a specified growing rank r(theta) retain this asymptote? Start by comparing the source operator-norm remainder with the next predicted singular value at that rank. This is needed for vanishing relative error. A suitable uniform remainder and a fully charged physical mode implementation remain missing.

## Related open work

- [PR3910](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3910) bounds forward physical Gaussian row norms; it does not compute this inverse singular spectrum.
- [PR371](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/371) accounts for final-grid rounding of Gaussian blocks; this result is exact-real and leaves that execution obligation open.
- [PR6413](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6413) reduces encoded finite recovery setup work; this proof supplies no setup implementation.
- [PR6459](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6459) sharpens constant-shift finite-cap inverse norm bounds; this varying-phase full-cell asymptote concerns a different matrix family and quantity.
- [PR6404](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6404) gives an exact truncated Gaussian cross-rim determinant and rank obstruction; no such truncation or Schur elimination occurs here.
- [PR6405](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6405) sharpens the truncated Gaussian Schur positivity range; it does not compute this full-cell approximation spectrum.

- [PR6482](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6482) changes signed residue packing and finite Gaussian recovery precision; it supplies no full-cell inverse singular spectrum or rank-error comparison.
- [PR6487](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6487) lowers bulk factor precision for cyclic-band solves; it preserves a complete solve and does not compute this fixed-rank compression error.

No shared computed number is compared with these PRs. The older merged PR5986 concerns polynomial inverse locality under norm hypotheses, which is also a different approximation contract.
